history.period: 1514 (current structure); site evidence 8th-11th century, earlier habitation to c. 3rd century BCE
history.summary: Hilltop fertility-goddess shrine on Yellammagudda, ~5 km from Saundatti (CSV town 'Belgaum' corrected: Belgaum/Belagavi is the district headquarters; the temple stands at Saundatti, Belagavi district). Current structure built in 1514 by Bomappa Nayaka (Naik) of Raibag/Raybag, but the site is much older: ASI-backed archaeological evidence dates parts to the Rashtrakuta-Chalukya period (8th-11th century) and pottery/tombs to c. 3rd century BCE-3rd century CE. Legend identifies Yellamma as Renuka, wife of sage Jamadagni and mother of Parashurama, whose beheaded head became the goddess. Architecture blends Chalukyan, Rashtrakuta and Jain influences; the complex includes shrines of Ganesha, Mallikarjuna, Parashurama, Eknath and Siddheshwara, plus three sacred tanks (Kumkum, Yoni, Arihan Kundam) and the Jogal Bhavi well believed to cure skin ailments. Saundatti was the first capital of the Ratta dynasty. Managed by the Government of Karnataka since 1975. Jatra season runs October-February, with the grandest gathering on Margashira Purnima (Bharat Hunnime); up to a million pilgrims from Karnataka, Maharashtra, Goa and Andhra Pradesh attend.

name: Saundatti Yellamma Temple
town_description: Saundatti (Savadatti) is an ancient town in Belagavi district, Karnataka, about 90 km from Belagavi city. It was the first capital of the Ratta dynasty and is the gateway to the hilltop Yellamma shrine, the Malaprabha river and nearby Saundatti Fort.

travel.road: ~90 km from Belagavi by road; temple on Yellammagudda ~5 km from Saundatti town

visitor_information.best_time: October-February (jatra season; peak on Margashira Purnima)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Weekdays 6:30 AM-4:30 PM and 6:30 PM-10:00 PM; weekends 6:30 AM-4:30 PM
